blocks.text: Zscaler's Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) uses signature-based detection to monitor your network for malicious activities and prevent attacks. Signature-based detection compares your traffic with predefined signatures (like fingerprints) of known network attack patterns and performs the specified action when there is a pattern match. Signatures uniquely identify the characteristics of specific types of network activities that indicate an intrusion or a threat of intrusion. The Zscaler service evaluates your network traffic against the signatures through the IPS Control policy. When a threat is detected based on a signature pattern match, the IPS enforces a preconfigured policy action to allow or block the traffic.

The Zscaler service uses signatures built and updated by ThreatLabZ (Zscaler's security research team), as well as signatures from industry-leading vendors. In addition to the signatures managed by Zscaler, you can create and deploy custom IPS signature rules to identify unique threats that are specific to your organization's requirements and threat landscape. You can rapidly deploy IPS signature rules when new threat intelligence information is available and swiftly mitigate potential attacks targeting your infrastructure. Custom IPS signatures can be created in the Zscaler Admin Console using Snort-like syntax, which supports a lightweight rules description language. These rules can be deployed in the Zscaler cloud without requiring any additional infrastructure and can be applied to both non-web and web (after decryption via SSL/TLS Inspection) traffic transiting the Service Edges for Internet & SaaS (ZIA), including Public, Private, and Virtual Service Edges.
Custom IPS signatures provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Define custom IPS signature rules in the Zscaler Admin Console based on the well-known Snort syntax and deploy your signatures on the Zscaler cloud without any additional infrastructure. Maintain control over your custom IPS signatures as private configurations that are accessible only to your organization.

Configure IPS Control policy rules based on custom signatures to monitor your network traffic for malicious activities and identify specific threats, and enforce condition-based actions on traffic transiting any Service Edge for Internet & SaaS.
Inspect both non-web and web (decrypted using SSL/TLS Inspection) traffic to detect threats that match your custom IPS signatures.

Leverage Zscaler logs to analyze and investigate threats detected in your network and build telemetry data for external systems, such as cloud security information and event management (SIEM), extended detection and response (XDR), or similar event collection tools and threat intelligence platforms. These logs can also serve for auditing purposes and help you ensure compliance.

blocks.text: The custom IPS signatures added for an organization are validated in two stages before deployment—static and dynamic validation. In static validation, the rules are checked for syntax errors, duplicate signatures, and are evaluated against several other metrics based on predefined conditions. Rules that pass the static validation go through a dynamic validation in which the signatures are run against designated packet captures to ensure efficient resource usage, optimal performance, and minimal costs. After validation, you can enable the custom IPS signatures to propagate them on the Zscaler cloud, and they are stored in the Zscaler Central Authority (CA) for each tenant separately. You can then define IPS Control rules using your custom signatures to detect threats that match the signatures and prevent network intrusion. The Service Edge for Internet & SaaS downloads your policies and custom signatures as part of your organization configurations from the CA and enforces matching policies inline on your user traffic transiting the Zscaler cloud.

Firewall and Web Insights provide visibility into the logs recorded for IPS traffic that matches with your custom IPS signatures. You can also track this data using interactive charts in the IPS Overview dashboard. Using Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS), you can stream your logs in real time from the Zscaler Nanolog to your SIEM system.

blocks.item: To enable Custom IPS Signature Rules for your organization, contact your Zscaler Account team.

You can define a maximum of 1,000 custom IPS signature rules. Before creating custom IPS signatures, Zscaler strongly recommends that you read the Specifications and Limitations for Custom IPS Signature Rules to understand the Snort-like syntax and features supported by Zscaler.

blocks.heading: About the Custom Signature Rules Page

blocks.text: On the Custom Signature Rules page (Internet Access > Resources > Custom IPS Signatures > Custom Signature Rules), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Search for a custom signature rule.
Import new custom signature rules or modify existing custom signature rules using a CSV file.
Export your custom signature rules to a CSV file.
Download a sample import CSV file, which can be used to import custom signature rules.
Click Promote All to initiate dynamic validation of all custom signature rules.
Add a custom signature rule.
Modify the table and its columns.
Show or hide the filters supported on the Custom Signature Rules page.
Filter the list of custom signature rules by Category and Status. You can select one or more values from the drop-down menu, and the list automatically updates to display relevant items.
View the list of all custom signature rules. By default, the table displays the following information:
Name: The name of the custom signature rule.
Description: The description of the custom signature rule.
Signature Rule: The custom signature rule using Snort-like syntax.
Threat Category: The threat category that is assigned to the custom signature rule. The custom signature rule can be used in an IPS Control rule via the assigned threat category.
Status: Status indicates the current position of the custom signature rule in the overall workflow.
Available Statuses
Promote Ready: Indicates that the signature rule is ready to be sent for dynamic validation. Rules that are saved after successful static validation are assigned this status.
Validation Pending: Indicates that the dynamic validation is currently in progress, which can take a few minutes.
Validation Failed: Indicates that the dynamic validation has failed. The rule must be modified and submitted for validation again.
Enable Ready: Indicates that dynamic validation is completed successfully and that the rule is ready to be enabled.
Enabled: Indicates that the custom signature rule is enabled and is ready to be used in IPS Control rules via the assigned threat category.

Disabled: Indicates that the rule is disabled. Signatures are continuously monitored by Zscaler to ensure the effective management of resources and a reliable experience for all organizations in the Zscaler cloud. Signatures found to cause resource overconsumption and potential performance issues might be temporarily disabled. To learn more, see Specifications and Limitations for Custom IPS Signature Rules.
Actions: The actions you can perform on the custom signature rules, such as editing and deleting.
Edit or delete a custom signature rule.
The custom signature rules are paginated with up to 500 rules displayed per page.
Go to the Threat Categories page.
